topics.topic: read_spooled_file identity/field validation: which request fields must match and whether mismatches are malformed vs unknown reference
questions: If `map_index` or `list_index` is present/absent in the wrong form for the actual producer node/port, is that a malformed request (`invalid_request`/`refused`) or `unknown_reference`?
If caller-supplied digest/size/media_type do not match the stored SpooledFile named by identity, should the call fail or ignore those descriptive fields?

quotes: A run or a node of its pinned version that does not exist is `unknown_reference`; a `map_index` given for a node that is not mapped, or absent for one that is, is `refused`; a well-formed element with no record yet is a result — not reached, or empty — never a refusal.

`read_spooled_file` takes only a SpooledFile — never a StoredValue — and names
it by its identity — `run_id`,
`producer_node_id`, `map_index` (omitted for a node that is not mapped),
`attempt_number`, `producer_port`, `list_index` (omitted for a `one`
port) — the lookup identity; its digest, size and media type only describe it
— an
identity naming no SpooledFile is `unknown_reference`;
judgement.divergence: Behavior A: the implementation validates `map_index`/`list_index` shape against the actual node/port form (and/or validates digest/size/media_type against the stored SpooledFile) and refuses malformed mismatches as `refused`/`invalid_request`. Behavior B: the implementation treats only the lookup identity as authoritative, returning `unknown_reference` when that identity finds no SpooledFile and ignoring digest/size/media_type mismatches. The MCP caller notices different refusal codes or success.
judgement.why: The text does not close how wrong optional identity-field form is classified for `read_spooled_file`, and it also leaves room for different handling of mismatched descriptive fields.

topics.topic: Pagination semantics for mutable records: what defines continuation/order when records change between pages
questions: For records that can change status (`runs`, `bindings`, `standing grants`), is their "store position" the creation position only, or does an update create a new position for paging/order?
If a record returned on page 1 changes and no longer matches the bound filter before page 2, does its token still name a valid continuation point for that filtered list?

topics.topic: Refusal reason schema: free-text vs closed symbolic reasons per operation
questions: Are refusal reasons free text, or a closed symbolic set per operation/check that callers/tests can rely on?

topics.topic: installation.load_installation duplicate agent_name handling: where rejected and via which refusal path
questions: Where is duplicate `agent_name` in configuration rejected, and with what refusal path?

topics.topic: list_records alias filters: whether executed_implementation/executed_binding matching must be kind-constrained
questions: When filtering by `executed_implementation` or `executed_binding`, is kind-constrained matching mandatory even if raw identifiers could collide in string form?

topics.topic: record_run_progress minimum payload: whether at least one new NodeExecution is required
questions: Must `record_run_progress` include at least one new NodeExecution, or may it legally write only derived run fields (status/waiting/output changes) with zero new executions?

topics.topic: runs.resume_run write ordering: when record_resumption is persisted relative to checking for service_unreachable waits
questions: Is `record_resumption` written only after confirming there is at least one `service_unreachable` wait, or always written before that check?

topics.topic: send_prepared_request for bindings with no outputs: whether response body must still be read/enforced against byte limits
questions: For a binding with no output ports, must the invoker still read/count response bytes and fail on `service_response_bytes_max`, or skip the body entirely?

topics.topic: store.read_records relation signatures: exact required args/order and error for extra irrelevant args
questions: For each named relation, what is the exact required argument list and order, and what exact error is returned for extra/irrelevant-but-well-typed arguments?
